'''Elantas GmbH''' (stylized as ELANTAS) is a manufacturer of [[Insulator (electricity)#Insulation in electrical apparatus|insulating materials]] for the electrical industry. It is headquartered in [[Wesel|Wesel, Germany]].

The company is wholly owned by [[Altana AG]]. ''Elantas'' operates through nine manufacturing companies in [[Europe]], [[Asia]], and [[South America]].

In August 2023, Altana AG announced that it had acquired 84.3% of the Swiss company [[Von Roll Holding AG]] via Elantas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ALTANA AG |first= |date=2023-08-11 |title=ALTANA AG erwirbt Mehrheitsbeteiligung an der Von Roll Holding AG von der Familie von Finck und kündigt öffentliches Kaufangebot an |url=https://www.altana.de/presse-news/details/altana-ag-acquires-majority-stake-in-von-roll-holding-ag-from-the-von-finck-family-and-announces-public-tender-offer.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=www.altana.de |language=de}}</ref> The acquisition was registered with the [[Federal Cartel Office]] on August 11, 2023, under B3-87/23. Approval was granted on September 8, 2023. Following the acquisition, Elantas recorded a 28 percent increase in sales to 878 million euros in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ALTANA AG |first= |date=2025-03-21 |title=ALTANA wächst 2024 zweistellig und investiert kräftig in die Zukunft |url=https://www.altana.de/presse-news/details/altana-waechst-2024-zweistellig-und-investiert-kraeftig-in-die-zukunft.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=www.altana.de |language=de}}</ref>

== History ==
Beck Electrical Insulation GmbH was founded in 1904 as a private company by Herrmann Josef Beck in [[Berlin]]. Beck was the first company to specialize entirely in varnishes and resins for electrical insulation in support of the emerging electrical industry in Germany.<ref name="elantas">{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228075120/http://www.elantas.de/fileadmin/altana/downloads/press/04_09_22_AEI_Beck_Jubilaeum_d.pdf|date=February 28, 2017|title=100 Jahre Beck – Jubiläum mit Fachtagung}}</ref> In 1936, his son, Hans-Joachim Beck, took over the company, which thereafter became known as Dr. Beck.

In 1948, following [[World War II]], the [[East Berlin]] plant was nationalized, marking a turning point for the company. In 1951, a new plant in [[Rothenburgsort|Hamburg-Rothenburgsort]], the company's current site, resumed operations.<ref name="elantas">{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228075120/http://www.elantas.de/fileadmin/altana/downloads/press/04_09_22_AEI_Beck_Jubilaeum_d.pdf|date=February 28, 2017|title=100 Jahre Beck – Jubiläum mit Fachtagung}}</ref>

In 1956, [[Unsaturated polyester resin|unsaturated polyester resins]] were introduced for the impregnation of electrical windings. The company expanded in 1956/57 by establishing branch plants in [[India]] (now ''Beck India Ltd.'') and [[England]].

In 1967, Hans-Joachim Beck retired from the business, which was then acquired by [[BASF]] as a branch of the former BASF Farben + Fasern AG.<ref name="elantas2">{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170227231651/http://www.elantas.de/fileadmin/elantas/companies/beck-india/EBIL-Marketing_Presentation_updated_Jan_2014.pdf|text=|wayback=|archiv-bot=|date=February 27, 2017|title=ELANTAS Beck India Ltd. Corporate Presentation}}</ref> In 1995, the plant underwent complete renovation and now uses modern manufacturing technologies to produce in an environmentally friendly manner.

In the course of a reorganization of BASF Coatings AG, Dr. Beck was transferred to Schenectady International Inc. New York, USA, in 1998. In 2003, the company, now operating under the name Beck Electrical Insulation GmbH, was taken over by Altana Chemie AG, Wesel, and as a subsidiary of Altana Electrical Insulation GmbH, it is Altana's European leader in the field of impregnating agents for electrical insulation.<ref name="elantas2">{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170227231651/http://www.elantas.de/fileadmin/elantas/companies/beck-india/EBIL-Marketing_Presentation_updated_Jan_2014.pdf|text=|wayback=|archiv-bot=|date=February 27, 2017|title=ELANTAS Beck India Ltd. Corporate Presentation}}</ref>

In 2004, Beck integrated large parts of the production and sales operations of Rhenatech GmbH Kempen, a subsidiary of Altana Electrical Insulation GmbH, into its Hamburg site, thereby strengthening its expertise in the field of casting compounds based on EP, PUR, and silicone resins. In 2005, Beck Electrical Insulation merged with Rhenatech and Wiedeking.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History of ELANTAS Europe {{!}} Electrical Insulation Solutions |url=https://www.elantas.com/europe/about-us/history-of-elantas-europe.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=Elantas}}</ref>
